CHIEF COMPLAINT::
Follow-up visit for ongoing breast cancer treatment.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS::
The patient is a 52-year-old female with stage II invasive ductal carcinoma 
of the left breast, ER+/PR+/HER2-. She was diagnosed on June 15, 2023 via 
core needle biopsy. Initial staging workup showed a 3.2 cm primary tumor 
with one positive axillary lymph node.

TREATMENT COURSE::
The patient initiated neoadjuvant chemotherapy on July 10, 2023.
She completed 4 cycles of Doxorubicin (Adriamycin) and
Cyclophosphamide every 3 weeks, with the last dose administered on 
September 18, 2023. She tolerated this phase well with manageable nausea 
and fatigue.

She then transitioned to Paclitaxel (Taxol) starting
October 2, 2023. Most recent infusion was yesterday.
She reports mild peripheral neuropathy
in her fingertips but states it is tolerable.

The patient also started Anastrozole 1mg daily on October 15, 2023 for 
endocrine therapy, which she will continue for 5 years post-treatment.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN::
The patient is responding well to neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Repeat imaging 
from last week shows significant reduction in tumor size to approximately 
1.5 cm. She will complete her remaining 4 weekly doses of Paclitaxel with 
the final infusion scheduled for November 27, 2023.

Signed by: Dr. Jane Smith, MD
Date: November 15, 2023 at 10:15 AM

CHIEF COMPLAINT::
Follow-up for ovarian cancer treatment.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS::
The patient is a 61-year-old female diagnosed with stage IIIC high-grade
serous ovarian carcinoma in November 2023. She underwent total abdominal
hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and optimal debulking
surgery on December 5, 2023.

TREATMENT HISTORY::
Postoperatively, the patient initiated adjuvant chemotherapy with
carboplatin AUC 5 and paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on January 8, 2024. She has
now completed 3 cycles of chemotherapy with treatments every 3 weeks.
Most recent infusion was on February 12, 2024. She is scheduled to receive
a total of 6 cycles.

The patient tolerates chemotherapy reasonably well. She experiences fatigue
for 3-4 days post-infusion and some mild nausea controlled with ondansetron.
No significant cytopenias noted on recent labs.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION::
Vitals: BP 118/72, HR 68, Temp 98.4\u00b0F
General: Well-appearing, no acute distress
Abdomen: Soft, well-healed surgical incision, non-tender
Extremities: No edema, no evidence of neuropathy

LABORATORY RESULTS::
CA-125 from last week: 42 (decreased from 156 at baseline)
CBC: WBC 4.2, Hgb 11.8, Platelets 185 - all within acceptable range

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN::
61-year-old female with stage IIIC ovarian cancer showing good response
to adjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy as evidenced by declining CA-125.

Plan:
1. Continue carboplatin/paclitaxel for 3 additional cycles
2. Next infusion scheduled for March 4, 2024 (cycle 4 of 6)
3. Repeat CA-125 with next cycle
4. After completion of chemotherapy, will discuss maintenance therapy options
5. Patient counseled on managing fatigue and maintaining nutrition

Signed by: Dr. Jane Smith, MD
Date: February 15, 2024 at 11:00 AM

[Report de-identified (Limited dataset compliant) by De-ID v.6.24.5.1]

REASON FOR CONSULTATION::
Management of metastatic melanoma.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS::
This is a 68-year-old male with history of stage IV melanoma originally 
diagnosed in May 2022. Primary site was right upper back with subsequent 
metastases to regional lymph nodes and lungs. BRAF V600E mutation positive.

PRIOR TREATMENT HISTORY::
The patient underwent wide local excision and sentinel lymph node biopsy 
on June 3, 2022. Pathology revealed 2.8 mm Breslow thickness with 
ulceration and 2 of 3 sentinel nodes positive.

He was initially treated with combination immunotherapy consisting of 
Nivolumab 1 mg/kg and Ipilimumab 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks. First infusion 
was on July 20, 2022. He received 4 doses with the last dose on 
October 5, 2022. Treatment was complicated by grade 2 colitis requiring 
steroid therapy, and immunotherapy was discontinued.

Due to progression on imaging 6 months ago (September 2023), he was 
switched to BRAF/MEK inhibitor combination therapy. He started Dabrafenib 
150 mg PO BID and Trametinib 2 mg PO daily on September 15, 2023. He has 
been on this regimen for approximately 6 months with good tolerance.

CURRENT STATUS::
Most recent CT scan from 2 weeks ago (February 23, 2024) shows partial 
response with 40% reduction in target lesions. Patient reports improved 
energy and resolution of dyspnea. He has experienced mild pyrexia and 
occasional chills, managed with acetaminophen.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION::
Vitals: BP 128/78, HR 72, Temp 98.8\u00b0F, RR 16
General: Alert, well-appearing male in no acute distress
Skin: Well-healed surgical scar on right upper back, no new suspicious lesions
Lymph nodes: No palpable cervical, supraclavicular, or axillary adenopathy
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN::
68-year-old male with stage IV BRAF-mutant melanoma demonstrating excellent 
response to targeted therapy with Dabrafenib/Trametinib combination.

Plan:
1. Continue current regimen of Dabrafenib and Trametinib
2. Repeat CT chest/abdomen/pelvis in 3 months (June 2024)
3. Monitor for skin toxicity and other adverse effects
4. Patient counseled on sun protection and self-skin examination
5. Consider switching back to immunotherapy if disease progression occurs

Electronically signed by: Dr. Jane Smith, MD,
Date: March 8, 2024 at 3:20 PM
